messages.text:
The tracking detector is now synchronized  to its latest baseline verison.



We need to insert a beampipe:

- let's assume a 0.8 mm Beryllium beampipe at 27 mm (first PR)



Then, make sure that (in a joint PR if necessary):

- a DD4hep model exists of BeamPipe + Tracker 
- a Acts Gen3 Tracking geometry following the DD4hep model
I’ll check the synchronized tracker baseline, add the beryllium beampipe in a first PR, then validate a combined DD4hep BeamPipe + Tracker model and its ACTS Gen3 geometry.

For the 0.8 mm wall at 27 mm, should 27 mm be the inner radius, the wall centre, or the outer radius? I recommend using the inner radius, giving outer radius 27.8 mm.
- Inner radius: 27.0–27.8 mm (recommended)
- Wall centre: 26.6–27.4 mm
- Outer radius: 26.2–27.0 mm

I’m using the acts-spack skill to verify the installed DD4hep/ACTS runtime. The primary checkout still has older local edits, so I’ll preserve those and work from the latest remote baseline in a separate checkout.

The tracker consolidation is merged into `main`. The existing acts-nodd adapter loads only the pixel DD4hep model and does not yet build a tracking geometry, so the second step needs real implementation. The Spack preflight reports changed setup fingerprints; I’ll verify the runtime before building.

I’m preparing the pipe with a 27 mm inner radius and 27.8 mm outer radius, pending your radius clarification. I’ll retain the inherited straight ±4 m extent and check its clearance to the tracker. For Gen3, sensor positions, axes and bounds will come from the constructed DD4hep model.

The baseline is available on `main`, and the work is isolated from your existing local edits. I’m adding the pipe as a separately testable component first, then assembling the tracker from its existing subsystem exporters.

The pipe builds successfully. The first native check exposed a ROOT material-handle error in the validator; I corrected it and am rerunning the checks. The pipe will include an explicit vacuum bore, and the tracker assembly will preserve each subsystem’s material recipes.

The pipe passes the native geometry checks: no overlaps, the expected 2.036 kg wall mass, and matching material paths for all 15 test rays. I’m checking Geant4 loading next. The ACTS adapter will derive sensor geometry from DD4hep while preserving the selected tracker layouts.

The first PR is ready: the pipe passes native validation and a one-event Geant4 smoke test. I’ll now assemble all six tracker readout systems. That includes reconciling shared service trunks so barrel and endcap exports don’t duplicate material in the same corridor.

The beampipe is published as [PR #57](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/57). The Gen3 implementation is underway in an isolated ACTS checkout. It preserves tilted strip frames, both faces of each strip pair, and individual pixel chip surfaces.

The assembly check found an identifier conflict: the pixel endcaps use systems 2 and 3, while the standalone short-strip barrel also uses 3. I’ll preserve pixel IDs and assign strips systems 4–7 in the combined compact, with a recorded translation from their standalone IDs. Module and sensor fields will stay unchanged.

The Gen3 adapter now compiles against the installed ACTS API. The full DD4hep model also builds. I’m testing their connection next; the combined audit includes the detailed supports and services as well as the sensor surfaces.

The existing pixel support and service apertures start at radius 27 mm, so a pipe with 27 mm inner radius and 27.8 mm outer radius intersects them. Which integration convention should I use?
- Keep 27 mm inner radius; enlarge only passive apertures to 28.8 mm (recommended, gives 1 mm clearance)
- Use 27 mm outer radius; retain existing apertures (nominal contact, no clearance)

The full audit found a physical clash: several existing pixel support and service apertures start at 27 mm, inside the proposed pipe’s 27.8 mm outer radius. I’ve put the aperture choice in the clarification above. All 45,646 sensitive elements match their source positions and axes; I’m continuing the software checks meanwhile.

The Gen3 alignment failure comes from wrapper volumes being centred on asymmetric sensor extents. I’m making those navigation volumes coaxial with the beam while preserving the sensor transforms. The service reconciliation also conserves the short-strip payload, with only floating-point rounding residuals.

Gen3 construction now succeeds: it has 117 navigation volumes and 45,646 unique sensitive surfaces. An independent comparison confirms every sensor’s source ID, centre, signed axes and dimensions. I’m testing propagation next; the passive-aperture decision remains pending.

All 128 seeded straight-track propagations completed and were saved. I’ve also prepared an isolated 28.8 mm passive-aperture candidate to assess the clearance fix before changing the baseline. It preserves sensors and conductor/cooling inventories, removing only support material and unused air around the pipe.

The clearance candidate passes the full DD4hep audit with zero overlaps. It enlarges 138 passive apertures and removes 10.13 g of support and unused-air material, while preserving sensors and conductor/cooling inventories. I’ll use this tested 1 mm clearance as the PR proposal and document it explicitly for review.

The beampipe PR is open. The combined model now preserves all 45,646 sensors and includes a tested 1 mm clearance around the pipe. I’m finishing the Gen3 checks and preparing the linked integration PRs.

The Gen3 construction and 128-track navigation check passed, as did all 385 ACTS C++ tests. The final material audit caught a remaining integration bug: two pixel cooling attributes still referenced the strip material names. I’m fixing those references and repeating the affected checks.

The cooling references are corrected, and the new regression tests catch the naming error, reflected sensor axes, and an incorrect pipe thickness. The final checks now cover the complete DD4hep model, Gen3 propagation, and Geant4 material recording. Passive support and service mapping remains a separate reconstruction task.

The final Gen3 and Geant4 checks passed: all 45,646 sensitive surfaces match the DD4hep inputs, and all 128 saved propagation probes completed. I’m publishing the ACTS companion PR and the stacked nODD integration PR; the separate beampipe PR remains first in the sequence.

The complete DD4hep suite passed: zero overlaps, matching sensor and material inventories, and 1 mm pipe clearance. PR57 has also been merged, so I’ll target the combined-model follow-up at main. The ACTS companion PR is open; I’m correcting its title to satisfy that repository’s CI convention.

Both follow-ups are published: nODD PR58 contains the complete DD4hep model, and ACTS PR3 contains the Gen3 adapter. Local validation is complete. I’m checking the hosted builds and closing the shared journal; exact token counters for this active turn remain unavailable.

The retained XML and library hashes still match the tested artifacts. PR58’s hosted build is running, and the ACTS title and lint checks have passed. The remaining ACTS platform builds are still queued or running.

PR58’s hosted build passed. The models and navigation checks are complete, and I’m publishing the final journal update. The PRs retain the provisional pipe length and radius convention, the passive-clearance amendment, and the remaining material-mapping and engineering work.

Implemented:

- [PR57](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/57): 0.8 mm Be pipe at **27 mm inner radius**; already merged.
- [PR58](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/58): complete **BeamPipe + Tracker DD4hep model**.
- [ACTS PR3](https://github.com/asalzburger/acts/pull/3): **DD4hep-derived Gen3 tracking geometry**.

Validated **45,646 matching sensitive surfaces**, **117 Gen3 volumes**, **zero overlaps**, and **128 completed propagation probes**.

Passive pixel apertures are enlarged to **28.8 mm**, providing 1 mm pipe clearance. Pipe length remains provisional at ±4 m.

Passive-material mapping remains separate work. Final hosted checks are running. Logs are updated; exact current-turn token counters remain unavailable.
